title: The /events page is 3.75 MB with 201 requests and paints a map tile last

source.ref: SEO, GEO and speed deep scan 2026-11-19 (production crawl of 3,000 URLs, all 720 sitemap pages, 8 crawler user agents, Lighthouse on 14 templates)

detail: The public /events page loads every event banner at upload size, starts Google Maps at once, and its largest paint is a map tile (Lighthouse simulated phone LCP 14.8 s, performance 46). Its description arrives in streamed metadata, so Lighthouse reports no meta description in the first bytes, and it has no og:url. Wanted: right-sized, lazy banners; the map only when it is near the screen or asked for; the description and og:url in the first response. SCAN-303 pins the five /events settings reads to one Promise.all: keep that. Fix (2026-11-20): event cards, the Around you cards and the Around you spotlight drew their banners as CSS backgrounds, which the browser fetches for every card in the DOM. They are now elements: lazy on the cards, eager with high fetch priority on the spotlight (the first photo), object-position keeping the host focal point. Stored uploads at their own size, never the paid optimizer. og:url now comes from pageContentMetadata (same clean path as the canonical, so every page-content route gains it). Re-tested: the map engine no longer starts on load (SCAN-904 gate plus the lightbox mounts MapCanvas only when open; the rail hides its own panel on /events); the LCP element named a map tile is the SVG door tile, which costs no request. The description already sits in for HTML-limited bots (Next streams metadata only to browsers); changing that site-wide is not part of this row. SCAN-303 Promise.all untouched.

verify.note: Fails on main: banners are CSS backgrounds and pageContentMetadata emits no og:url. Passes when banners are lazy img (spotlight eager), the map engine is a lazy chunk mounted on open, and og:url is set.
